title: The complex suppliers transfer to the exact DFT: θ = 1 − 7009/10⁷ (7.009·10⁻⁴) for the exact discrete Fourier transform (no new κ)
body:
Adds `research/exact-dft-transfer/` and one workflow; **no existing file changes and no new κ.** It records that this repository's complex suppliers are *batched networks* in the sense of eumemic's [exact-dft-bounds](https://github.com/eumemic/exact-dft-bounds) (`notes/batched-dft-note.tex`, `6f87d1a`), so each certified complex moment root `a` gives, in the exact complex-arithmetic model of OpenAI's *An explicit power saving for the exact discrete Fourier transform* (25 September 2026, `openai/math` at `adc7f12`), an exact DFT of every length and an exact complex convolution in

    O( n (log n)^θ (log log n)^(4−θ) ),   θ = 1 − a.

eumemic's repository proves this for the PR #144 supplier on main (a = 607/1250000). This package adds the two later suppliers; the same two propositions are [eumemic/exact-dft-bounds#1](https://github.com/eumemic/exact-dft-bounds/pull/1) (`c92cf70`).

## Result

| Supplier | Certificate | m | W / vertex | Deficit | Max child | a (certified) | θ |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| PR #144 (main `d1d6c07`) | `certificates/paired-cube-complex-input.json` | 72 | 29,937 | 1,936 | 60 | 607/1250000 = 4.856·10⁻⁴ | eumemic's value |
| PR #200 (`a1175449`) | `research/paired-cube-diagonal-bit-168/certificate.json`, `complex.profile` | 66 | 13,163 | 1,320 | 20 | 3327/5000000 = 6.654·10⁻⁴ | +37% |
| **PR #194 (`a8c8778`)** | `research/source-assisted-v4/certificate.json`, `complex_profile` | 66 | 12,052 | 1,320 | 20 | **7009/10⁷ = 7.009·10⁻⁴** | **+44%** |

For every fixed κ < 7009/10⁷ the exact DFT and exact convolution take O(n (log n)^(1−κ)) operations. OpenAI's saving is about 2.1·10⁻¹³.

## Argument

- The batched moment Σ_ρ N_ρ (ρ/m)^θ < W with θ = 1 − a is exactly this repository's coarse-saving moment Σ_ρ n_ρ ρ (m/ρ)^a < W m (|G| cancels). So a supplier's complex saving is the DFT exponent saving, up to the slightly weaker exp/log bounds used here (which is why PR #200's 6.65489…·10⁻⁴ is certified as 6.654·10⁻⁴).
- **PR #200 is a batched network** (Proposition B in `PROOF.md`, by reference): the shared-core word is retained from #144; the fused scalar word's complete signed identity is replayed on every formal column in both shear signs, which is the one-column identity that eumemic's Lemma 2.2 extends to every f; each operation carries one rational frame shared by both registers with nested chains, so each transition is adapters around one child of width its rank increment (Lemma 4.1); reuse pairs, terminal sinks and fused outputs are gates; the ledger Σ ρ n_ρ = 867438 = 66·13163 − 1320 is re-counted by that package.
- **PR #194 is a batched network** (Proposition C, by reference to `notes/source-assisted-note.tex` and the PR #194 checkers): the complete transcript is a linear word z_final = Mz + Lx with M invertible, each operation an exact local map with dyadic coefficients or a source control (gates); reads subtract the recomputed dirty response at frame zero, K + B = I is checked exactly, every auxiliary is brought to the full frame and every gate reversed (the one-column identity, replayed by the independent scalar transcript with mutation controls); the flow is monotone along nested frame chains with an acyclic once-only reuse DAG, so each transition is adapters around one child of its Fourier rank; Σ ρ n_ρ = 794112 = 66·12052 − 1320.

## Verify

    python3 -B research/exact-dft-transfer/verify.py --check     # stdlib only, about 20 seconds; -O is refused

The script checks every pin in `SOURCE.json` (the main certificate of PR #144 and the vendored certificates of PR #200 and PR #194, byte for byte as `git show <commit>:<path>`), rebuilds the three child histograms from those certificates and compares them with the committed `certificates/network-children-*.json`, checks the ledger identities (rank sum, deficit = Wm − rank = 2v − 3ℓ, largest child < m), certifies the batched moment at each claimed saving in exact rational arithmetic (artanh series with tail bound; exp(x) ≤ 1 + x + x²/(2(1 − x/3))), rejects the next 10⁻⁷ grid point for each supplier, and compares with `expected.json`. Margins: 3.16·10⁻³, 2.69·10⁻³, 5.27·10⁻⁴. The workflow runs `--check` on Python 3.11 and 3.14.

Run before opening: `--check` passes on this branch (Python 3.14, macOS). Not run: the full `make verify` (no existing file changes).

## Scope and limits

- Conditional on the suppliers' constructions exactly as in eumemic's note: exact complex phases, the Cayley cover and completed-core sharing are written arguments; scalar identities, frame nesting, ranks and ledgers are checked by the packages' scripts. For PR #194 the scalar transcript replay checks the one-column identity but does not materialize the physical Clifford transports.
- The multiplication bound's bit, assembly, routing, precision and Turing-machine interfaces are not used (item-by-item replacement in Section 6 of eumemic's note).
- Not formally verified; astronomically large constants; nothing here changes any κ.
